3.summary: This rule explains who can set up a One Person Company in India. Only a real human being who is an Indian citizen can start one or act as a nominee. Minors cannot be involved in these companies at all.
points: Only an Indian citizen who is a natural person can set up a One Person Company or be a nominee.
A person cannot be a member or a nominee in more than one One Person Company at the same time.
Minors cannot become members, nominees, or hold shares with a beneficial interest.
A One Person Company cannot be formed or converted for charitable objects under section 8.
Such a company cannot carry out Non-Banking Financial Investment activities.
3.example: Aarav, an Indian citizen, wants to start his own business. He decides to set up a One Person Company called Aarav Crafts Private Limited. Since he is a natural person and an Indian citizen, he is eligible to do so. Aarav cannot start or be a nominee in any other One Person Company at the same time, and he must ensure no minor is added as a member or nominee.

terms.meaning: A real human being, as opposed to a company or legal entity.
A person chosen to take the place of the sole member if needed.
A person who has not reached the age of majority.

3.watch: People often confuse residency rules, but the text specifically requires staying in India for a set period during the previous financial year.

4.summary: When setting up a One Person Company, the founder must choose a nominee who will take over if the founder dies or cannot make a contract. This rule explains how that nominee is added during registration, how the nominee can withdraw, and how the founder can change the nominee later. It also tells the company what forms to file with the official registrar.
points: The person starting a One Person Company must name a nominee and get their written consent.
The name of the nominee and their consent must be included in the company's incorporation forms.
If the nominee withdraws, the sole member must pick a new nominee within fifteen days.
The company must inform the Registrar using the specified forms and pay the required fees when a nominee changes or withdraws.
If the nominee becomes the new member due to the founder's death or incapacity, that new member must also name a new nominee within fifteen days.
4.example: Aarav decides to start a single-person business called Apex Techno Solutions Private Limited. Before setting it up, he asks his sister Priya to be his nominee in case he passes away or cannot legally make contracts. Priya agrees in writing. Aarav includes Priya's name and her written consent in the company's registration forms filed with the Registrar. Later, if Priya decides to step down as the nominee, she must send a written notice to Aarav and the company.

terms.meaning: A company that has only one person as a member.
A legal condition where a person is not able to enter into valid contracts, such as due to loss of mental soundness.
The official government authority responsible for registering companies.

4.watch: Make sure to file the required forms and get written consent from the nominee within the timelines stated in the text.

6.summary: A One Person Company can change into a private or public company by updating its core documents and meeting the required number of members and directors. The company must apply using a specific form with the necessary fees and updated documents. Once the Registrar checks everything and is satisfied, they will approve the change and issue a certificate.
points: The company must alter its memorandum and articles by passing a resolution.
It must increase its members and directors to the required minimum and maintain the correct paid-up capital.
The company must file an application in e-Form No. INC-6 with the altered documents and fees.
The Registrar will review the latest audited financial statement and issue a certificate upon approval.
6.example: Aarav owns Apex One Person Company. He decides to convert it into a private company to bring in a business partner. He increases the number of members and directors to meet the legal requirements, updates his company documents, and submits e-Form INC-6 with the required fees. The Registrar examines the latest audited financial statement, ensures all rules are followed, and issues the certificate for the conversion.

terms.meaning: The fundamental documents that set out the constitution and rules of a company.
The total amount of money that shareholders have paid to the company in exchange for shares.
The government official responsible for registering and overseeing companies.

6.watch: A One Person Company cannot be converted into a company registered under section 8 for charitable objects through this process.

7.summary: A private company, except a charity company, can turn into a One Person Company if all members and creditors agree in writing and the shareholders pass a special resolution. The company must then submit the resolution and an application with the required documents to the Registrar of Companies. Once checked and approved, the Registrar will issue a certificate.
points: Pass a special resolution in a general meeting to start the conversion.
Get written no-objection letters from all members and creditors before passing the resolution.
File the special resolution with the Registrar within thirty days.
Submit an application with updated documents like the memorandum, articles, creditor approvals, and a directors' affidavit.
7.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited wanted to change its business structure into a One Person Company. First, the owners obtained written no-objection letters from every member and creditor. Next, they held a meeting where the shareholders passed a special resolution approving the change. Within thirty days, they filed this resolution with the Registrar of Companies. Finally, they submitted an application through e-Form INC-6, attaching their updated memorandum, articles, creditor letters, and a directors' affidavit confirming everyone agreed. After reviewing the latest audited financial statement, the Registrar approved the form and issued a new certificate.

terms.meaning: A formal decision made by shareholders that requires a high majority vote.
The government official who handles company registrations and records.
A written statement confirmed by oath or affirmation for use as evidence.

7.watch: Charity companies registered under section 8 are not allowed to use this rule to convert into a One Person Company.

8A.summary: This rule explains when a company name is considered undesirable and will not be allowed. It lists specific types of names, such as those that are offensive, too similar to existing companies or trademarks, or misleading about the company's business activities. Promoters must avoid these forbidden names when setting up a company.
points: A name cannot include certain protected emblems or registered trademarks unless proper permission or consent is given.
A name cannot be offensive, misleading about financial activities, or use words like 'British India' or names of foreign embassies.
A name cannot be identical or too similar to an existing company, limited liability partnership, or reserved name.
A name cannot consist only of a continent, country, State, city, or commonly used descriptive words for an activity.
8A.example: The promoters of Sunshine Enterprises Private Limited wanted to name their new firm Haryana Limited. Under the rules, this proposed name is not allowed because it contains only the name of a State. To fix this, they decided to change the name to Sunshine Haryana Traders Private Limited, which includes other words and is acceptable under the law.

terms.meaning: A special symbol, word, or phrase legally registered to represent a company's goods or services.
The people who take the initial steps to plan and set up a new company.
A company that is controlled by another larger company known as the holding company.

8A.watch: Just because a word is not explicitly banned does not mean any name is allowed if it resembles existing registered names or trademarks.

8B.summary: This rule lists certain special words and expressions that you cannot use in a company name without getting permission first from the Central Government. These restricted words include names of government bodies, leaders, courts, and specific schemes. The rule ensures that a private company name does not sound like an official government body or authority.
points: You cannot use words like Board, Commission, Authority, or Undertaking in a company name without Central Government approval.
Words related to government and governance, such as National, Union, Central, Federal, Republic, President, and Governor, require prior approval.
Using names of leaders, ministers, courts, municipal bodies, and specific entities like Khadi and Village Industries Corporation needs prior approval.
Using the word Scheme with government names, India, Bharat, or any government scheme requires prior approval.
8B.example: A group of friends in Mumbai wanted to start a new business to sell handmade goods. They decided to name their venture 'National Khadi and Village Industries Corporation Private Limited'. Because the text states that words like National and Khadi and Village Industries Corporation cannot be used in a company name without getting previous approval of the Central Government, the friends must obtain this approval before they can officially register their company with that specific name.

terms.meaning: The main national government of the country.
A group of words forming a particular phrase.

8B.watch: A common confusion is thinking that getting approval from a local office is enough, but the text specifically requires the previous approval of the Central Government.

9A.summary: This rule allows you to extend the time period for a reserved company name using a government website. You must pay specific fees within certain time limits before the original reservation expires. The Registrar also keeps the power to cancel the reserved name under the Act.
points: You can extend a reserved company name by paying fees through the official web service.
Pay one thousand rupees before twenty days expire to extend the name up to forty days.
Pay two thousand rupees before forty days expire to extend the name up to sixty days.
Pay three thousand rupees before twenty days expire to also extend the name up to sixty days.
9A.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited successfully reserved its company name through the web service. Before twenty days passed from the approval date, the founders decided they needed more time to complete their paperwork. They paid a fee of one thousand rupees through the website before the twenty-day deadline, successfully extending their name reservation up to forty days from the original approval date.

terms.meaning: A government official who handles company registrations and records.
A web service used for incorporating a company electronically.

9A.watch: People often confuse the different fee amounts and their exact deadlines for extending the reserved name.

12.summary: To register a new company, you must file an online application using a specific electronic form along with the required fee to the local Registrar. If your business needs approval from a sector regulator like the Reserve Bank of India, you must get it before doing those activities and declare it when incorporating. If you are starting a Nidhi company, you need a special Central Government declaration before beginning your business.
points: File the incorporation application with the Registrar where your registered office will be located.
Use the electronic form SPICe+ along with the prescribed fee.
Obtain and declare any needed approvals from sectoral regulators before pursuing those business objects.
A Nidhi company must get a Central Government declaration under section 406 before starting business.
12.example: Aarav wants to start a finance business called Nidhi Wealth Private Limited in Mumbai. Since it is being incorporated as a Nidhi, the company must obtain the required declaration from the Central Government under section 406 of the Act before it starts its business operations. Aarav submits the incorporation application through the electronic form SPICe+ to the local Registrar along with the fee, and includes the necessary declaration stating that they will obtain the required government approval before commencing business.

terms.meaning: The government official appointed to handle company registrations.
Government authorities that oversee specific industries, like the Reserve Bank of India.
A specific type of company formed to cultivate the habit of thrift and savings among its members.

12.watch: Make sure to obtain all required sectoral approvals and declarations before starting your business activities.

14.summary: When starting a company, certain professionals must give a formal written statement. This rule states that the statement given by an advocate, chartered accountant, cost accountant, or company secretary must be in a specific official form called Form No. INC.8. It also explains the specific laws that define these professions.
points: Professionals like advocates and accountants must use Form No. INC.8 for their declaration.
This rule applies to the process of starting a company under section 7 of the Act.
Definitions for the professionals are borrowed from their respective governing acts.
14.example: A group of entrepreneurs wants to start a new business named Sunrise Ventures Private Limited. They need help with their company incorporation paperwork. They hire an independent Chartered Accountant in practice to provide a formal statement confirming that all legal requirements for forming the company have been met. To follow the law correctly, the Chartered Accountant must submit this required statement using the official Form No. INC.8.

terms.meaning: A formal written statement made by a professional.
The legal process of forming a new company.

14.watch: Make sure to use Form No. INC.8 specifically, rather than any other general form.

15.summary: This rule explains how people starting a new company must officially declare certain things under the Companies Act, 2013. Every person who signs to set up the company and every first director must submit this declaration. The document must be given in a specific official format called Form No. INC-9.
points: Applies to every subscriber to the memorandum.
Applies to every first director named in the articles.
Must be submitted in Form No. INC-9.
15.example: Aarav and Priya decided to start a new business named Sunrise Ventures Private Limited. Aarav signed the main founding document as a subscriber, and Priya was named as a first director in the articles. Because of this rule, both Aarav and Priya must individually submit a declaration using the specific official format known as Form No. INC-9 during the incorporation process.

terms.meaning: The people who sign the primary founding document to create the company.
The initial members chosen to manage the company, named in the articles.
The specific official form required for the declaration.

15.watch: Do not confuse this declaration form with other incorporation documents, as it specifically must be Form No. INC-9.

16.summary: When starting a company in India, certain details about every person or company signing up as a founder must be given to the Registrar. This rule lists all the specific information and identity proofs needed for both individuals and corporate bodies. It ensures the government has accurate records of everyone involved in setting up the new business.
points: Individual founders must provide personal details like name, parents' names, date of birth, educational qualification, and income-tax PAN.
Founders must also submit recent photographs, contact details, identity proofs, and residential proofs that are not more than two months old.
If a founder is a body corporate or another company, it must provide its registration numbers, address, and a copy of the board resolution or partner agreement.
Founders who already have an updated Director Identification Number do not need to attach proof of identity and residence.
16.example: Aarav Sharma wants to start a new business named Sharma Technologies Private Limited. As a subscriber to the memorandum, Aarav must submit his personal details, a recent photograph, his educational qualification, his PAN card, and an electricity bill that is less than two months old to the Registrar. If Aarav already holds a valid and updated Director Identification Number, he does not need to attach his identity and residence proofs.

terms.meaning: A government official appointed under the Companies Act who handles company registrations.
A person or body corporate that signs the founding document to form a company.
A company or legal entity, which can include foreign companies and limited liability partnerships.

16.watch: People often confuse the rule by thinking residential bills can be of any age, but utility bills must not be more than two months old.

19.summary: This rule explains how a person or group can apply to start a new charitable company under section 8 without using the words Limited or Private Limited in its name. The applicants must submit a specific electronic form along with the required fee, memorandum, and articles of association. They also need to provide professional declarations and an estimate of future income and expenses for the next three years.
points: Apply using the SPICe+ form and pay the required fee to the Registrar.
Prepare the memorandum of association in Form No. INC.13.
Attach the memorandum, articles of association, and applicant declarations.
Include a declaration from a qualified professional confirming compliance with the law.
Provide a three-year estimate of future income sources and spending objects.
19.example: Asha and Kabir wanted to start a charitable organization named Help Hands to promote education. Instead of naming it Help Hands Private Limited, they decided to apply for a section 8 license. They filled out the SPICe+ form, prepared their memorandum in Form No. INC.13, and attached an estimate of their income and expenses for the next three years. A practicing Chartered Accountant reviewed their documents and gave a declaration that all legal requirements were met. They submitted everything along with the proper fee to the Registrar.

terms.meaning: A foundational document that sets out the constitution of a company and its objects.
The government authority responsible for registering companies.
A document that contains the rules for internal management of a company.

19.watch: Do not forget to include the professional declaration confirming that all legal requirements for registration have been met.

20.summary: An existing limited company with charitable objects can apply for a special license to drop the words 'Limited' or 'Private Limited' from its name. To do this, the company must submit an application with required documents, pay a fee, publish a public notice, and wait for the Registrar to make a decision. The Registrar checks financial records, considers any objections, and decides whether to grant the license.
points: The company must apply in Form No. INC.12 with the required fee.
The application needs documents like the e-Memorandum, financial statements, and professional declarations.
The company must publish a notice in a vernacular newspaper, an English newspaper, and on notified websites.
The Registrar reviews financial reports, audit reports, and any objections before deciding on the license.
20.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited is an existing company that wants to work purely for charity. To remove 'Private Limited' from its name, it applies to the Registrar using Form No. INC.12 and pays the fee. It attaches its articles, asset statements, and a professional declaration. The company also publishes a notice in a local vernacular newspaper and an English newspaper. After checking the financial statements and ensuring no objections are raised within the time limit, the Registrar decides whether to give the license.

terms.meaning: An officer appointed under the Act to keep company records and handle registrations.
A document that sets out the main objects and constitution of a company.
A newspaper published in the local language of the district.

20.watch: Make sure to publish the notice in both a local language newspaper and an English newspaper as required.

21.summary: A company formed for charitable purposes under Section 8 of the Companies Act can change into another type of company by following specific rules. The company must pass a special resolution at a meeting and provide a detailed explanation of the reasons. It also needs to file paperwork and seek approval from the proper authorities.
points: The company must pass a special resolution at a general meeting to approve the conversion.
The meeting notice must include a detailed statement explaining why the company wants to change, its history, objects, and current benefits.
The company must file copies of the resolution and notice with the Registrar.
The company must apply to the Regional Director for approval to convert and send an intimation to the Registrar.
21.example: Asha Welfare Private Limited, a company originally set up for charity, decided it wanted to change into a regular business company. To do this, the members held a general meeting and passed a special resolution. They prepared a notice with an explanatory statement detailing their incorporation date, main objects, reasons for the change, and any tax exemptions or land they received at concessional rates. They then filed the required forms and documents with the Registrar and the Regional Director to seek official approval for the conversion.

terms.meaning: A formal decision passed by a high majority of company members at a meeting.
The fundamental document that sets out the company's constitution and main objects.
The government official responsible for registering and overseeing companies.

21.watch: Do not confuse simply holding a meeting with also needing to file the required forms with the Regional Director and Registrar.

22.summary: This rule explains the steps a charitable company must follow when it wants to change into a normal company. It must publish public notices, inform various government authorities, and get approval from the Regional Director. After getting approval, it must update its documents and inform the Registrar to complete the conversion.
points: The company must publish a notice in a local vernacular newspaper, an English newspaper, and on its website.
It must send copies of the application and notice to specific government authorities like the Income Tax Department and the State Chief Secretary.
The Board of directors must give a declaration that no company income or property was given away as dividends or bonuses to members.
The company must clear its dues, and any remaining balance of accumulated profits must be transferred to the Investor Education and Protection Fund.
After getting approval, the company must hold a general meeting, pass a resolution, and file the required documents with the Registrar to get a fresh certificate.
22.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited, a charitable company, decided to change into a regular company. It published a notice in two local newspapers and on its website. The directors declared that no company property was ever distributed as dividends to members. They sent copies of the application to the Income Tax Officer and the Chief Secretary. After clearing all debts, they transferred any leftover unutilized income to the Investor Education and Protection Fund. Finally, they received approval from the Regional Director, held a meeting, and filed the amended documents with the Registrar to get a new certificate.

terms.meaning: A newspaper published in the principal local language of the district where the company's office is located.
A government authority appointed to oversee various company law matters under the Act.
A legal document that sets out the constitution of a company and its relationship with shareholders.

22.watch: Do not confuse the Regional Director who approves the conversion with the Registrar who registers the final documents.

23A.summary: This rule explains how a company must file a specific declaration to start its business under the law. A director must use a special form and have it checked by a qualified professional. If the company needs special approval from a regulator, that approval must also be attached.
points: A director must file the declaration using Form No.INC-20A.
The filing follows the rules for registration offices and fees.
A practicing Company Secretary, Chartered Accountant, or Cost Accountant must verify the form contents.
If the company needs approval from a sectoral regulator like RBI or SEBI, that approval must be attached.
23A.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited wants to start its business operations. To do this lawfully, a director of the company fills out Form No.INC-20A. Because the company deals in a sector that needs special clearance, the directors also obtain the required registration approval from the Reserve Bank of India. They attach this approval to the form. Finally, a practicing Chartered Accountant verifies the contents of the form before it is officially filed according to the registration and fee rules.

terms.meaning: A person who helps manage and run a company.
Official bodies that watch over and control specific industries, like the Reserve Bank of India.

23A.watch: Do not forget to attach approvals from regulators like RBI or SEBI if your specific business needs them.

25A.summary: This rule requires certain older companies to submit their details and registered office particulars using a specific electronic form. Companies that have missed filing certain financial statements or annual returns cannot use this form unless there is a management dispute recorded. If a company fails to file this form, it will be marked as non-compliant and blocked from making certain changes.
points: Companies created on or before December 31, 2017, must file e-Form ACTIVE.
Companies with pending financial statements or annual returns are restricted from filing unless they have a recorded management dispute.
Struck off, liquidating, amalgamated, or dissolved companies do not need to file.
Failing to file results in being marked as ACTIVE-non-compliant and blocks specific corporate changes.
Filing the form late requires a fee of ten thousand rupees to become compliant again.
25A.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited was incorporated in November 2017. Because it missed filing its required annual returns with the Registrar, it was initially restricted from filing e-Form ACTIVE. However, the company had a severe management dispute, which the Registrar duly recorded in the register. With this dispute on record, Meera Textiles Private Limited was allowed to proceed. After paying the required fee of ten thousand rupees, the company successfully submitted its particulars and was marked as ACTIVE Compliant.

terms.meaning: An official appointed under the Act to keep company records.
Official reports showing the financial position and performance of a company.

25A.watch: Companies often confuse the exemption for struck-off or dissolving companies with active companies that simply forgot to file.

25B.summary: The Registrar can physically visit a company's registered office to check if it is real and working. During the visit, the Registrar will take photos, check documents with two local witnesses, and prepare a report. If the office cannot receive mail, the Registrar can start steps to remove the company's name.
points: The Registrar visits the company office using info from the MCA 21 portal.
Two independent local witnesses and sometimes the local police must be present.
The Registrar takes a photograph of the office and collects documents from the occupant.
If the office cannot receive communications, a notice is sent to remove the company name.
25B.example: An official visits Sunshine Agro Private Limited based on records found on the MCA 21 portal. The official brings along two local witnesses and takes a photograph of the office building. They check the rent agreement and speak with the person present at the location to ensure the company actually operates from that address and can receive mail.

terms.meaning: An official appointed to maintain the register of companies.
The online portal used by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for company filings.
Corporate Identity Number, a unique number given to a company.

25B.watch: People often confuse a physical verification visit with a routine tax audit, but this rule is only about checking the official registered office address.

27.summary: This rule explains how a company must inform the authorities if it moves its registered office to a new location. The company needs to fill out a specific form, pay a fee, and attach the same documents and verification methods that were required when the company was first started. It ensures the government has the correct and verified address for official notices.
points: File a notice of change in Form No. INC.22.
Pay the required fee along with the form.
Attach the same documents used for address verification during incorporation.
Follow the same manner of verification specified under section 12(2) of the Act.
27.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited decided to move its office to a new building across town. To make this legal, the directors filled out Form No. INC.22 and included the required fee. Along with the form, they attached the exact same type of ownership proof and verification documents that they had submitted when the company was first incorporated, as required by the law.

terms.meaning: The official main address of a company where legal notices and mail are sent.
The legal process of forming a new company.
The process of proving that information or a document is true and correct.

27.watch: Do not forget to attach the exact same verification documents used during incorporation.

30.summary: When a company wants to move its registered office from one State to another, it must apply to the Central Government using a specific form and include documents like its updated memorandum and minutes. The company also needs to list its creditors, notify them through advertisements and letters, and send a copy of the application to the State's Chief Secretary. The Central Government will then review the request, hold hearings if there are objections, and pass an order either approving or rejecting the move.
points: File the application in Form No. INC.23 with the Central Government along with the required fee, memorandum copy, meeting minutes, and board resolution or power of attorney.
Provide a list of creditors and debenture holders signed by the company secretary and at least two directors, stating that no employees will be laid off due to the move.
Advertise the proposed shift in a vernacular and an English newspaper, and send individual notices to each creditor, debenture holder, the Registrar, and regulators.
The Central Government will issue an order approving or rejecting the shift within fifteen days if there are no objections, or after hearings if objections exist.
30.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited decided to move its registered office from one State to another. To do this, the directors filed Form No. INC.23 with the Central Government along with their updated memorandum and a list of creditors. They published a notice in both an English and a local language newspaper and sent notices by post to all their creditors. They also served a copy of the application to the Chief Secretary of their current State. Since no one raised any objections, the Central Government reviewed the paperwork and passed an order approving the shift.

terms.meaning: The foundational document that sets out the company's constitution and objectives.
A person or entity that holds a bond or certificate of loan issued by the company.
Fired or laid off from employment.

30.watch: Shifting is not allowed if any inquiry, inspection, investigation, or prosecution is pending against the company under the Act.

33A.summary: If a company does not change its name within three months of receiving a direction to do so, its name automatically changes to a specific code starting with ORDNC. The Registrar then updates the official register and gives the company a new certificate of incorporation. This rule does not apply if the company's name change application is still pending review, unless that application is later rejected.
points: A company must follow a direction to change its name within three months.
If it fails, a new default name using ORDNC, the year, a serial number, and its CIN becomes its name automatically.
The Registrar updates the register and issues a fresh certificate of incorporation.
The company must update its registered office details and display a specific warning statement under its new name until it changes it properly.
33A.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited received a government direction to change its name. Three months passed, and the company did not change its name, nor did it have any pending name change application. Automatically, its name changed to an ORDNC code with its year and serial number. The Registrar issued a fresh certificate of incorporation. Now, Meera Textiles Private Limited must print the statement about the uncomplied order below its name everywhere it appears, until it properly alters its memorandum.

terms.meaning: A unique identification number given to a company by the government.
An official document issued to prove that a company has been officially registered.
The fundamental document that sets out a company's basic rules and name.

33A.watch: People often confuse the automatic name change with a regular voluntary name change, but this happens by law without any action from the company if it misses the three-month deadline.

34.summary: Under Rule 34, a company must give copies of certain important documents to its members when they ask for them and pay a fee. These documents include the memorandum, articles, and specific resolutions or agreements. The company has seven days to send these copies after receiving the request.
points: A member must pay a fee to get the documents.
The company must send the documents within seven days of the request.
The documents include the memorandum, the articles, and certain agreements or resolutions.
34.example: Aarav is a shareholder in ABC Private Limited. He wants to read the company rules and writes a letter to ask for a copy of the articles and the memorandum, along with the required fee. The company receives his letter. Within seven days, ABC Private Limited must mail those copies to Aarav.

terms.meaning: The main document that sets up a company and defines its relationship with shareholders.
The document that contains the internal rules for running the company's business.
A person who owns shares in the company and is listed as a member.

34.watch: Remember that the seven-day countdown starts only after the member makes the request and pays the fee.

35.summary: Under this rule, official papers and notices can be sent to a company, its officers, the Registrar, or a member using electronic methods like email or fax. These electronic messages must go to specific addresses provided for this purpose and must create a saved record that can be printed out. The rule also explains how delivery by courier and post works.
points: Documents can be sent to a company or officer using electronic transmission.
Electronic transmission includes email, fax, or designated message boards with verification systems.
Documents can also be sent to the Registrar or any member through electronic transmission.
Delivery by post is considered complete after forty-eight hours for a meeting notice, or at the normal delivery time for other cases.
35.example: Ahmad wanted to send a meeting notice to Zenith Electronics Private Limited. Instead of using regular mail, Ahmad sent an email to the exact email address that Zenith Electronics had officially provided for receiving messages. Because the email was sent to the right address and created a saved record that could be printed, the service of the document was successfully done through electronic transmission.

terms.meaning: Sending messages electronically like by email or fax to a provided address, or posting on a designated network.
An official government authority who handles company registrations and records.
Something that can be touched and read in physical form, like printed paper.

35.watch: Make sure you only use the exact email address or fax number that the company or officer has officially provided.

38.summary: This rule explains how to use an electronic form called SPICe+ to set up a new company. It covers details like how to fill out the main application, how to submit founding documents, and what happens if the Registrar finds mistakes in your paperwork. You can use it to apply for names, director numbers, and your registered office all at once.
points: To start a company, you must file the SPICe+ electronic form along with your electronic Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association.
The form allows you to apply for up to three Director Identification Numbers and lets you propose only one name for the company.
If the Registrar finds defects in your application, you will be given time to fix and re-submit the documents.
The Registrar will issue a Certificate of Incorporation in Form No. INC-11 once the company is successfully registered.
38.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited wanted to start its business using the online incorporation process. The founders filled out the SPICe+ electronic form along with their e-MoA and e-AoA, proposing a single name for the company. They also applied for three Director Identification Numbers through the same form. When the Registrar checked the application, a small error was found. The Registrar informed the founders, who corrected the mistake and re-submitted the paperwork within the given time limit so the company could receive its certificate.

terms.meaning: Simplified Proforma for Incorporating Company Electronically Plus (Form INC-32), the main online form used to set up a company.
A founding document that sets out the constitution of a company and its relationship with shareholders.
A unique identification number allotted to an individual who intends to be a director of a company.

38.watch: Do not assume fees or timelines apply universally without checking the specific text exemptions for certain small capital or member counts.

39.summary: Certain companies can change their structure to become a company limited by shares. To do this, the members must pass a special resolution and meet the required share capital amount. The company must then submit the correct forms and documents to the Registrar of Companies.
points: Charitable companies under section 8 cannot use this rule to convert.
The new share capital must be equal to the previous guarantee amount.
Members must pass a special resolution to change the Memorandum and Articles of Association.
Two forms, MGT14 and INC27, must be filed with the Registrar of Companies along with fees and a list of members.
39.example: Meera Guarantee Limited wanted to change its structure into a company limited by shares. The members held a meeting and passed a special resolution to remove the guarantee clause and update their rules. They ensured their new share capital matched their old guarantee amount. Next, they filed Form MGT14 and Form INC27 with the Registrar of Companies, along with their updated Memorandum and Articles and a list of members holding the required shares. After checking the complete application, the Registrar approved it and issued a certificate of incorporation in Form INC11B.

terms.meaning: A decision agreed upon by a high majority of company members at a meeting.
The foundational document that governs a company's relationship with the outside world.
The government official who handles company registrations and records.

39.watch: Note that charitable companies formed under section 8 are not allowed to use this conversion rule.

40.summary: This rule explains how a company applies to change its financial year. It requires filling out a specific electronic form along with reasons, board meeting details, and past application history. The Regional Director reviews the request and may ask for corrections before approving or rejecting it.
points: An application to change the financial year must be filed in e-Form No. RD-1 with the required fee.
The applicant must provide reasons, board meeting minutes, a Power of Attorney or Memorandum of Appearance, and details of any past applications made within the last five years.
If the application is defective, the applicant gets fifteen days to fix it and can re-submit up to a maximum of two times.
The Regional Director will either approve, reject, or issue an order within thirty days, and if no action is taken, it is deemed approved.
The final approval order must be filed with the Registrar in Form No. INC-28 within thirty days of receiving it.
40.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited wants to change its financial year. The company fills out e-Form No. RD-1 and attaches its reasons, the board meeting minutes showing the vote count, and details of any applications from the past five years. The Regional Director reviews the form and finds a small error, sending an email intimation to correct it. Meera Textiles fixes the error and re-submits the form within fifteen days. The Regional Director approves the request and sends an order. Finally, Meera Textiles files this order with the Registrar using Form No. INC-28 within thirty days.

terms.meaning: An official of the central government who handles various company law approvals.
A legal document giving someone the authority to act for another person or company.
An authority who keeps records of companies registered under the law.

40.watch: Do not assume the application is denied if the official misses the thirty-day deadline, because it is automatically deemed approved.

41.summary: This rule explains the steps a public company must take to convert into a private company. The company must file an application with the Regional Director using a specific e-form along with required documents, lists of creditors, and declarations. It also requires publishing advertisements and sending notices before the application can be reviewed for approval.
points: The application must be filed with the Regional Director within sixty days of passing a special resolution.
The company must attach copies of its updated articles and memorandum, meeting minutes, and declarations from a key managerial personnel or director.
A list of creditors and debenture holders must be attached along with a supporting affidavit.
The company must advertise the proposed conversion in newspapers and send individual notices to creditors, debenture holders, and authorities at least twenty-one days before filing.
41.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited wants to change from a public company to a private company. First, the shareholders pass a special resolution in a general meeting. Next, the company prepares its updated memorandum, a list of creditors, and required declarations. Before filing the application with the Regional Director, Meera Textiles publishes an advertisement in a local vernacular newspaper and an English newspaper, and sends notices by registered post to all its creditors and debenture holders at least twenty-one days in advance.

terms.meaning: An authority appointed by the Central Government to handle certain company law administration tasks.
A decision made by shareholders that requires a higher vote percentage than a normal decision.
Top officers of a company such as the chief executive officer, managing director, or company secretary.

41.watch: Make sure to publish the newspaper advertisements and send notices at least twenty-one days before filing the application.

1.summary: This rule gives a short title to a specific set of company regulations in India. It states that these regulations are officially known as the Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014. They became active starting from the first day of April, 2014.
points: The rules are called the Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014.
They came into force on April 1, 2014.
1.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited was setting up its business paperwork in India. The founders wanted to know the official name of the foundational rules they needed to follow for setting up their company. Their legal advisor told them that the regulations are called the Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014, and that they came into force on April 1, 2014.

terms.meaning: to officially become active and start applying
the official short name by which a law or rule is known

1.watch: Do not confuse the title of these rules with the main Companies Act itself.

2.summary: This rule gives the basic meanings of certain words and terms used in the incorporation rules of companies. It explains what words like Act, Form, and Regional Director stand for throughout these rules. It also clarifies that any words not specially defined here will take their meaning directly from the main Companies Act.
points: The word Act refers to the Companies Act, 2013.
Form or e-Form means any official form specified and notified by the Central Government.
Regional Director is a person appointed by the Central Government in the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.
Words not defined in these rules take their meaning from the Act or related rules.
2.example: Aman wants to start a new business called Sunrise Traders Private Limited. When he fills out an official document to register his company, he uses the electronic document specified by the government. Because the rules state that Form means an e-Form notified by the Central Government, Aman knows he is using the correct paperwork required under the law.

terms.meaning: An attachment or added document at the end of the rules.
A specific person appointed by the Central Government in the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.

2.watch: Do not assume terms not defined here have everyday meanings; check the Companies Act first.

7A.summary: This rule sets the penalties if a One Person Company or its officers break any part of these rules. The punishment includes a primary fine and an extra daily fine if the mistake continues. Every officer involved can be held responsible.
points: Applies to a One Person Company or any of its officers.
Triggered when someone breaks the rules.
Includes a main fine up to five thousand rupees.
Includes an extra fine up to five hundred rupees for each day the rule-breaking continues after the first day.
7A.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited is set up as a One Person Company. Its director, Rahul, fails to follow a procedure required under the incorporation rules. Because Rahul broke the rule, the company and Rahul become punishable with a fine of up to five thousand rupees. If Rahul continues to ignore the requirement after the first day, they will also face a further fine of up to five hundred rupees for every extra day the violation goes on.

terms.meaning: Breaks or acts against a rule or law.
A person in a position of authority in the company, such as a director.

7A.watch: People often think the daily fine stops automatically, but it continues for every single day the violation is not fixed.

8.summary: This rule explains when a new company name is considered too similar to an existing company name. When checking for similarity, certain common differences like punctuation, plural forms, and business types are ignored. If the compared names become the same after ignoring these items, the new name is not allowed unless a special permission is given.
points: Words like Private, Limited, and LLP are ignored when comparing company names.
Differences in plural forms, letter spacing, punctuation, and tenses do not make names different.
Phonetic spellings, misspellings, domain extensions, and word order are also disregarded.
An existing company can allow a similar name by passing a Board resolution.
8.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited applied for a company name. An existing company is named Meera Textiles Limited. Under the rules, words like Private and Limited are ignored during comparison. Because the core names are identical after ignoring those words, the new name is deemed to resemble the existing company too nearly.

terms.meaning: Spellings that sound the same when spoken aloud.
A formal decision made by the board of directors of a company.
Writing words using the alphabet of another language based on similar sounds.

8.watch: People often think changing punctuation or adding 'Pvt. Ltd.' makes a name unique, but the law treats it as the exact same name.

9.summary: This rule explains how to apply for a company name or a change of company name using specific online government services. You must submit your request through the official website along with the required fee. The Registrar will then review your application and can either approve it or reject it.
points: Apply to reserve a new company name using the online SPICe+ service on the MCA website.
Apply to change an existing company name using the online RUN service.
Pay the required fee as stated in the registration and fees rules.
If there are defects, you get a chance to fix and resubmit the form within fifteen days.
9.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited wanted to change its company name. The directors used the online RUN web service on the official website to submit their request along with the prescribed fee. After reviewing the application, the Registrar found some minor errors in the paperwork. The Registrar allowed Meera Textiles Private Limited to fix the defects and resubmit the web form within fifteen days, ensuring they had a fair chance to correct their application before a final decision was made.

terms.meaning: The government official who handles company registrations.
The act of fixing mistakes or defects.

9.watch: Do not confuse the SPICe+ service used for new names with the RUN service used only for changing names.

10.summary: If a company's articles contain special restrictions called entrenchment provisions, the company must inform the Registrar about them. New companies do this by submitting specific forms with the required fee when they are being set up. Existing companies must file a specific form within thirty days from the date the entrenchment provisions are added.
points: New companies must give notice of entrenchment provisions in specific forms along with the fee during incorporation.
Existing companies must file Form No. MGT.14 within thirty days from the date of entrenchment.
The required fee is provided under the Companies (Registration offices and fees) Rules, 2014.
10.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited is a newly forming company whose rulebook, known as the articles, includes entrenchment provisions that make certain rules very hard to change. When applying to incorporate the company, the founders must submit Form SPICe+ and pay the prescribed fee to notify the Registrar about these special provisions.

terms.meaning: The rulebook that governs how a company is managed internally.
Special provisions that make certain rules in the company's articles much harder to change than usual.
The government official who keeps records of companies.

10.watch: Do not confuse the filing process for a new company at the time of incorporation with that of an existing company changing its rules later.

11.summary: This rule allows companies to choose standard sets of internal management rules called model articles. A company can use these rules completely or just in part, depending on what fits its situation. These model tables are found in Schedule I of the law.
points: Companies can adopt model articles from Tables F, G, H, I, and J.
Adoption can be total or partial depending on the company type.
11.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited is starting its business and needs to set its internal rules. Instead of writing a completely new document from scratch, the directors decide to use the standard rules provided in Table F of Schedule I. They review the table and adopt most of the provisions as they apply to their company, choosing to use the model articles in totality for their business operations.

terms.meaning: Standard sets of rules provided by the law for how a company should be managed.
Using something entirely or completely.

11.watch: Do not assume every company must use the exact same table, as different tables apply to different types of companies.

13.summary: This rule explains how the foundational documents of a company must be signed. It covers rules for regular subscribers, illiterate persons, corporate bodies, and foreign nationals. Every signature must follow specific verification and witnessing steps.
points: Each subscriber must sign in the presence of at least one witness who verifies their identity.
Illiterate subscribers may use a thumb impression, which must be explained and authenticated by another person.
Bodies corporate and limited liability partnerships must authorize a representative through a resolution to sign.
Foreign nationals residing outside India must have their signatures and identity proofs notarized and certified according to their country.
13.example: Aarav is setting up Apex Solutions Private Limited. He signs the memorandum and articles of association in front of a witness named Priya, who verifies his identity details, dates the document, and signs as a witness. Priya also adds her name, address, description, and occupation on the papers as required by the rules.

terms.meaning: The fundamental documents that set up a company and define its rules and objectives.
A person who agrees to take shares and helps form the company.
A legal term for a company or corporation.

13.watch: Make sure the person signing for a company or limited liability partnership is duly authorized by a resolution.

17.summary: When starting a company, the people named as the first directors must share their details and their interests in other businesses. They also need to give their agreement to serve as directors. All of this must be submitted using a specific form along with the required fee.
points: List the details of each person named as a first director in the articles.
Include information about their interests in other firms or bodies corporate.
Obtain and file their consent to act as a director.
Submit everything using Form No. DIR.12 with the prescribed fee.
17.example: Aarav and Vivaan decided to start a new business named Sunrise Ventures Private Limited. Since their names were written in the articles as the first directors, they had to prepare their personal details and note their interests in other companies. They both signed a paper agreeing to take on the role of directors. Finally, they submitted Form No. DIR.12 along with the correct fee to complete the filing process as required.

terms.meaning: The official document that sets out the rules for running the company's internal affairs.
Legal entities or companies formed under law.
Official agreement or permission to do something.

17.watch: Do not forget to include details about the director's interests in other firms along with their consent.

18.summary: This rule explains how a company receives its official proof of registration, known as the Certificate of Incorporation. The Registrar must issue this certificate using a specific form. The certificate will also show the company's permanent account number if the Income-tax Department has given one.
points: The Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation.
The certificate uses Form No. INC-11.
The certificate includes the company's permanent account number if provided by the Income-tax Department.
18.example: Asha Cosmetics Private Limited completes all its paperwork to register as a new company. The Registrar approves the documents and issues the official Certificate of Incorporation using Form No. INC-11. Because the Income-tax Department already gave the company a permanent account number, that number is printed directly on the certificate.

terms.meaning: The official document given by the government that proves a company legally exists.
The government official responsible for registering companies.
A unique identification number given for tax purposes.

18.watch: This rule does not state that the Registrar must create the permanent account number, only that it is mentioned if the Income-tax Department already issued it.

25.summary: When a company needs to verify its official address, it must submit a specific form with a fee. Along with this form, the company must also provide official proof that it is allowed to use the building. This proof can be an ownership document, a rental agreement, an owner's permission letter, or a recent utility bill.
points: File Form No. INC.22 along with the required fee to verify the registered office.
Attach proof of the premises using one of four accepted document types.
Accepted proofs include title deeds, a notarized lease agreement with a recent rent receipt, owner authorization, or a recent utility bill.
25.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited is setting up its official business location. To complete the address verification, the company fills out Form No. INC.22 and pays the required fee. Since the company does not own the building, the directors attach a notarized copy of their lease agreement along with a rent receipt that was paid within the last month. This fulfills the official rule for verifying their registered office address.

terms.meaning: The official main address of a company.
A copy of a document verified as authentic by a legal notary public.
Services like electricity, gas, or telephone supplied to a building.

25.watch: Make sure the utility bill or rent receipt is fresh and within the time limits mentioned in the rule.

26.summary: Every company with a website must publish its basic details on the home page. These details include its name, address, Corporate Identity Number, and contact info. The Central Government can also require the company name to be printed on other documents later.
points: Applies to any company that has a website.
Must show company name, registered office address, and Corporate Identity Number.
Must display telephone number, fax number if any, email, and a contact person for queries.
All these details must appear on the landing or home page of the website.
26.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited runs a website for its business. According to the rules, the company must clearly display its name, registered office address, Corporate Identity Number, telephone number, fax number if applicable, email, and the name of a contact person for queries right on its home page. If visitors land on the main page, they will easily find all this required information.

terms.meaning: A unique identification number given to a company when it is registered.
The main home page of a website that visitors see first.

26.watch: People often forget to include the contact person's name for queries on the home page.

28.summary: This rule explains how a company can move its registered office from the area of one Registrar of Companies to another within the same State. The company must apply to the Regional Director using a specific form with fees, required documents, and declarations. Finally, the approved order must be filed with the State Registrar.
points: File Form INC.23 with the Regional Director along with fees and necessary documents.
Include a Board resolution, a Special Resolution of members, and required declarations about dues, creditors, pending cases, and employee interests.
The Regional Director passes an order approving or rejecting the complete application within fifteen days.
File the certified copy of the approval order in Form INC-28 with the State Registrar within thirty days.
28.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited wanted to move its main office from Mumbai to Pune, which changed its Registrar of Companies within the same State. The company prepared Form INC.23, attaching a Board resolution and a special resolution passed by its members. The directors signed a declaration stating all worker dues were cleared and creditors agreed. After submitting the papers, the Regional Director reviewed the complete application and approved the move. Within thirty days of getting the certified order, Meera Textiles filed Form INC-28 with the State Registrar.

terms.meaning: An authority appointed by the Central Government to oversee certain company matters.
A decision approved by a high majority of company members.
Top officers of the company such as the chief executive or chief financial officer.

28.watch: Do not confuse moving an office within the same Registrar's jurisdiction with moving it to the jurisdiction of a different Registrar, which requires this specific Regional Director approval.

29.summary: A company cannot change its name if it has missed filing its annual returns or financial statements, or if it has not paid back matured deposits, debentures, or interest. However, the name change is allowed once the company clears these pending filings or payments. To apply for the change, the company must submit an application with the required fee, and it will receive a new incorporation certificate.
points: A company with pending annual returns or financial statements cannot change its name.
A company that has failed to repay matured deposits, debentures, or interest cannot change its name.
The restriction is removed once the necessary documents are filed or payments are made.
To change the name, file an application in Form No. INC.24 with the fee.
A new certificate of incorporation in Form No. INC.25 is issued after the name change.
29.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited wanted to change its name to Meera Garments Private Limited. However, the company had not yet filed its annual financial statements with the Registrar and had unpaid matured deposits. Because of this, the Registrar did not allow the name change. Once Meera Textiles filed all pending financial statements and repaid the matured deposits, it applied using Form No. INC.24 along with the fee. The Registrar then approved the request and issued a new certificate of incorporation in Form No. INC.25.

terms.meaning: The government official who keeps records of companies.
A type of loan instrument issued by a company.
An official document proving a company is legally formed.

29.watch: People often think a company can change its name while filings or deposit repayments are still pending, but they must be completed first.

31.summary: When a company changes its registered office from one State to another, the Central Government must approve it. The company must file this approval order with the Registrar of the old State within thirty days. You must also include the required fee.
points: Get a certified copy of the Central Government order approving the office transfer.
File this order using Form No. INC.28.
Submit it to the Registrar along with the fee within thirty days of receiving the order.
31.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited decided to shift its registered office from Maharashtra to Gujarat. After getting the approval, the Central Government sent a certified copy of the order to the company. Following the rules, Meera Textiles quickly filed Form No. INC.28 along with the required fee to the Registrar within the thirty-day limit.

terms.meaning: The main document that sets up a company and states its basic details.
The official government authority that handles company registrations and records in a State.

31.watch: Remember that the thirty-day countdown starts from the day you receive the order, not the day it was signed.

32.summary: If a company raises money from the public through a prospectus and has unused money left, it cannot change how that money is used without following specific steps. The company must pass a special resolution through a postal ballot. The notice for this change must contain detailed information such as the amount received, the amount used, and the reasons for the change.
points: A company with unutilized public money cannot change its application objects without a special resolution passed by postal ballot.
The notice of the resolution must include total money received, money utilized, and the unutilized amount.
The notice must explain the proposed change, its justification, the amount for new objects, and the estimated financial impact.
Details of the resolution must be published as an advertisement at the same time postal ballot notices are sent, and the notice must be placed on the company's website if it has one.
32.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited raised money from the public using a prospectus to build a factory, but some money remains unutilized. The company now wants to use this remaining money for a new purpose instead. To do this legally, Meera Textiles must send a postal ballot notice to its shareholders to pass a special resolution. This notice must clearly state how much money was originally received, how much was spent, the reasons for changing the plan, and the expected financial impact on the company's earnings.

terms.meaning: An official document inviting the public to buy shares or debentures.
A decision made by shareholders that requires a high voting majority.
A way of voting by post or electronic means rather than at a physical meeting.

32.watch: People often confuse changing objects with simply spending the money on the originally stated goals.

33.summary: This rule explains how a company changes its type between private and public. To make any such change, an application must be filed using a specific form with a fee. If a public company becomes a private company, extra steps and documents are needed.
points: To convert a private company to a public company or the other way around, file Form No. INC.27 with a fee.
When turning a public company into a private company, you must get approval from the Regional Director first.
For this conversion, you must include the service number of the approval form, the altered memorandum and articles, and a fee.
You must file these documents within fifteen days of receiving the order from the Regional Director.
33.example: Alpha Public Limited Company decided to change its structure and become a private company. After receiving the approval order from the Regional Director, Alpha Public Limited Company filed Form No. INC.27 along with the altered e-Memorandum of Association, the e-Article of Association, and the required fee. They submitted all these documents to the Registrar within fifteen days of getting the order.

terms.meaning: A type of company with restricted share transfers and limits on the number of members.
A type of company that is not a private company and allows the public to hold its shares.
An official who keeps records of companies under the law.

33.watch: Make sure to file the paperwork within the fifteen-day limit after receiving the approval order.

37.summary: This rule explains how an unlimited liability company can change into a company with limited liability by shares or guarantee. The company must pass a special resolution, publish notices to invite objections, send notices to creditors, and submit an application with required documents to the Registrar. Certain conditions apply, such as keeping the same company name for one year after conversion.
points: The company must pass a special resolution in a general meeting to start the conversion.
Within seven days, the company must publish a notice in two newspapers and send a copy to creditors and debenture holders.
Interested persons and creditors can send objections within twenty-one days of the notice publication.
The company must file an application with the required documents and declarations within forty-five days of passing the special resolution.
The company cannot convert if its net-worth is negative, if pending inquiries exist, or if certain other defaults apply.
37.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited, an unlimited liability company, wants to convert into a company limited by shares. First, the members gather and pass a special resolution. Within seven days, the company publishes a notice in an English newspaper and a local language newspaper, and also sends notices to its creditors by speed post. After collecting all required declarations, a certified list of creditors, and required documents, Meera Textiles files its application with the Registrar within forty-five days to complete the conversion process.

terms.meaning: A decision approved by a high majority of company members in a meeting.
The local language spoken in the specific district where the company office is located.
A person or entity that has lent money to the company and holds a certificate of debt.

37.watch: Make sure to note that the company cannot change its name for a full year after the conversion is complete.

38A.summary: When a new company applies for incorporation, it must send an extra form along with its main application. This form, called AGILE-PRO-S (INC-35), is used to ask for important business registrations and services like tax numbers and a bank account. It includes several items that became effective on different dates mentioned in the rules.
points: Companies apply for registration using e-form AGILE-PRO-S (INC-35).
The form includes applications for GSTIN, EPFO, and ESIC registrations.
It also covers Profession Tax Registration, opening a bank account, and Shops and Establishment Registration.
38A.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited is newly setting up its business operations. To complete its setup smoothly without filing separate paperwork for everything, the founders submit e-form AGILE-PRO-S (INC-35) along with their main company incorporation application. Through this single form, Meera Textiles Private Limited simultaneously requests its Goods and Service Tax Identification Number, Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation registration, Employees’ State Insurance Corporation registration, Profession Tax Registration, Shops and Establishment Registration, and the opening of a bank account.

terms.meaning: The legal process used to form a new company.
An electronic form used for official submissions.

38A.watch: Do not assume that this form is optional or that you can use a different form number for these specific registrations.
